summary: The contradiction argument is valid. The limit of near-vertical near-minimizers yields a nonzero planar normal and controls the strictly positive-side mass. The irrational-kernel case follows from the marginal centerpoint condition and the anchor-fiber centroid bound. In the rank-one case, the finite tilts correctly control both closed ray masses, while convexity, Brunn--Minkowski, Grünbaum's inequality, and the accepted log-concave threshold lemma establish the required uniform lower bound on the mass contributed by the boundary-line fibers. The constant estimate q_d>1/15 and the final rearrangement both correctly contradict t<W/64. All hypotheses and boundary-mass cases are accounted for.
